Recorded because it is the ONE handler that deviates from the committed input convention, and a reviewer must not read that as an oversight.

GAP (probe origin + transport) — the plan never says how the three live proofs reach the server or where setup learns the base URL, and Task 12.1 (STATE: NOT_STARTED) is what teaches the session its origin (scripts/serve.py:217 writes `options.baseURL`). RESOLUTION: the proofs go DIRECT over bounded node:http with stream:false — GET {origin}/v1/models; one POST {origin}/v1/chat/completions carrying response_format json_schema for the schema proof; parallel.maxReaders concurrent trivial POSTs for the slot proof — and the ORIGIN is an INPUT to handleSetup, computed by the impure caller as resolveBaseUrl(routerCfg, upstreamCfg, createFailoverState()) (router-client.ts:95). Tests pass a local ephemeral stub's origin. Reasoning: this makes 12.2 implementable and fully testable BEFORE 12.1, keeps the origin derivation in one place, and honours the wire-notes:41-55 DRIFT by never routing a probe through opencode's prompt path.

GAP (the schema proof checks a capability the pipeline no longer uses) — §2.1:630 proves 'the served model answers one tiny schema-constrained request', but Task 0.2's DRIFT (wire-notes:41-55) already re-scoped the harness's structured output to prompt-shaped + independent validation, so nothing downstream depends on response_format. RESOLUTION: keep the proof exactly as the plan writes it (it is cheap, and a server that rejects response_format outright is a server worth knowing about), and define PASS as 'the reply body validates against the probe schema' rather than 'the server echoed a response_format field' — a model that ignores the constraint but answers correctly passes, which is the honest reading of 'answers one tiny schema-constrained request'. Recorded so a reviewer does not read the retained proof as a contradiction of the DRIFT.

GAP (what 'smoke-spawned' means) — §2.1:628 says every configured command is smoke-spawned, but spawning `ctest` or `pytest` bare would RUN the target repo's whole suite at setup time, and spawning `node` bare hangs on a REPL. RESOLUTION: the smoke check spawns [argv[0], "--version"] with shell:false, childEnv, closed stdin and a short kill timeout, and FAILS only when the process could not be spawned at all (spawnSync's `error` set — ENOENT/EACCES). A non-zero exit is explicitly NOT a setup failure. Reasoning: the failure mode the plan names is 'an unspawnable test command', not 'a command that dislikes its arguments'; `--version` is understood or harmlessly rejected by all four pinned runners, and either way the SPAWN is what is being measured. Recorded because a stricter reading (exit code 0 required) would fail `go --version` on a perfectly good toolchain.

GAP (setup's asks are not §2.11 questions) — core/types.ts:85-93 has no setup origin and adapter/questions.ts:89 needs a runDir. RESOLUTION: the two asks are returned in handleSetup's RESULT and surfaced by the session as the §6.2:1875 sanctioned interactive ask; NO question record is written and QUESTION_ORIGINS is NOT widened. Asserted as zero writes so a later implementer cannot 'helpfully' add an origin.

GAP (buildCommand) — §2.1:483-485 and adapter/evidence.ts:338-342 both support a per-scope buildCommand, but SCHEMAS.Config omits it under additionalProperties:false (types.ts:530-540). RESOLUTION: detection NEVER proposes a buildCommand; the ctest fixture's config carries only {command, timeoutMs, itemTest}. Reasoning: the schema is the thing that validates persisted config, so emitting the field would write a config that fails its own validation gate. Recorded as a §2.1-vs-SCHEMAS.Config inconsistency for the Phase 12 gate; adding buildCommand to the schema is a §2 schema change and is NOT taken here.

GAP (scope commands, as opposed to itemTest templates) — §2.1:499 pins the four itemTest DEFAULTS but never pins the full-scope `command`. RESOLUTION, per ecosystem: node -> package.json `scripts.test` tokenized with core/shell-parse shellTokens when present, else ["node","--test"]; pytest -> ["pytest"]; go -> ["go","test","./..."]; ctest -> ["ctest"]; cargo -> ["cargo","test"]. The itemTest template is attached ONLY when detectRunner(proposed command) returns the profile that template belongs to — so a package.json whose test script is `jest` gets its real command and NO node itemTest (the §2.1:487-497 absent-template fallback covers it) rather than a silently wrong `node --test {files}`. timeoutMs = the §2.1:483 example 600000 for every proposed scope.

GAP (ctest needs a build directory) — a bare `ctest` at a repo root finds no test suite in most CMake projects, and the plan proposes no detection for the build dir. RESOLUTION: propose ["ctest"] unqualified and leave it to the user's config edit; do NOT invent a build-dir probe and do NOT emit a buildCommand (see above). Reasoning: the smoke check only proves ctest is spawnable, the §2.1 detection is explicitly a PROPOSAL, and guessing `build/` would be a silent wrong answer where an obviously-incomplete one is honest. Raised at the Phase 12 gate as the weakest leg of the matrix.

GAP (requiredScopes) — Config.verify.requiredScopes is REQUIRED (types.ts:554) and the plan never says what detection proposes. RESOLUTION: one entry per detected scope; with exactly ONE detected ecosystem the pattern is "**"; with several, each entry's pattern is that ecosystem's proposed source glob, so no path is left with an empty scope list by construction. An empty requiredScopes array is never written (it would leave every path unverified while validating cleanly).

GAP (cargo) — the §2.1:620 detection list names Cargo.toml, but no cargo itemTest template, no cargo behavioralPaths proposal and no cargo RUNNER_PROFILE exist (evidence.ts:57-118). RESOLUTION: propose command ["cargo","test"], NO itemTest (the absent-template fallback applies), behavioralPaths ["src/**"] (the Rust layout convention), and add NO runner profile — detectRunner's conservative node fallback (:137) bins an unfamiliar cargo failure as `error`, which is the safe bin. Adding a fifth RUNNER_PROFILE is a §2.6.1 classification change and is not taken here.

GAP (go behavioralPaths 'minus') — §2.1:525 proposes '**/*.go minus **/*_test.go', which core/shell-parse globMatch (:425) cannot express and Config.verify.behavioralPaths (string[] of positive globs) cannot hold. RESOLUTION: propose ["**/*.go"] and make the mandatory behavioralPaths confirmation ask NAME the *_test.go caveat so the user can narrow it. Reasoning: widening globMatch with negation would change semantics for its three consumers (freshness, planning, gates-edit) — a far larger blast radius than one over-broad proposal the user is already required to confirm.

GAP (models.default) — every Config field except the two asked ones is supposed to be defaulted, but a served model id cannot come from prose (§2.1:602's `qwen3.6-27b` is this repo's weight). RESOLUTION: setup adopts the single id from the live /v1/models list when the list has exactly ONE entry; when the caller supplied a model id (Task 12.1 knows the session's model), it adopts that and the §2.1:629 proof then verifies it; otherwise setup FAILS with the §2.1:634 named remedy ('several models are served — set models.default in .conductor/config.json'). Reasoning: this keeps the question count at the plan's two, never guesses among several weights, and makes the §2.1:629 proof non-vacuous in every branch.

GAP (proof failure vs a written config) — §2.1:620-624 reads 'writes this file. Setup then proves every assumption it just recorded'. Taken literally, a failed proof leaves a written config, repoConfigured flips true, and every gate opens on an UNPROVEN config. RESOLUTION: the proofs run against the CANDIDATE config in memory and the atomic write happens only after every check passes; a failed proof leaves the repo unconfigured. Reasoning: §2.1:634 makes a failed check a setup FAILURE, and gates-phase.ts:246 keys the whole tool surface off the file's presence — a half-proven config on disk is strictly worse than no config.

GAP (repoConfigured on a corrupt config) — with the reader introduced here, what does a present-but-invalid .conductor/config.json mean? RESOLUTION: readWorkspaceConfig returns null on absent, unparseable, OR validate("Config") failure, and repoConfigured is exactly `readWorkspaceConfig(root) !== null` — so a corrupt config reopens setup rather than opening every gate on an unvalidated object. ONE exported derivation, consumed by handleSetup and by whatever supplies legalTools' repoConfigured, so gate and handler can never disagree (the C-037 ruling-1 principle).

GAP (pytest spawnability, C-003) — §2.1:499 pins ["pytest","{files}"] as the default, but bare `pytest` is NOT on PATH on this machine (CORRECTIONS.md:27-35). RESOLUTION: the §2.1 template stays the FIRST choice; when its argv[0] fails the smoke spawn, detection falls back to [<python3>, "-m", "pytest", "{files}"] (and the scope command to [<python3>, "-m", "pytest"]) — evidence.detectRunner:130-132 already recognises the `python… pytest` argv shape as the pytest profile, so the swap costs nothing downstream. This is a fallback, not a silent rewrite: the proposal returned to the user names which form was chosen and why.

GAP (format rules) — the plan says nothing about detecting formatters, and §2.1:558 ships `rules: []`. RESOLUTION: setup proposes format.rules: [] and detects no formatter. The smoke-spawn row still covers format-rule commands, because a RECONFIGURE of a config that already has rules must smoke-spawn them.

GAP (the 'initialize a repo here' branch) — §3.9:1500-1502 offers `git init` as one of the two choices, but adapter/gitio.ts exports read queries only (:119-282); there is no write call at HEAD. RESOLUTION: the init leg is a new gitio write (`git init`) under gitio's execFileSync-argv + GIT_ENV discipline, performed by the HANDLER (never a model session — core/gates-git.ts already denies session-side git writes), after which setup re-derives isRepo and continues down the ordinary git-repo path in the SAME call. Covered by row 12.2-nogit-offer's second leg.

GAP (scope of the task, recorded from the launch context) — 12.2 touches NO serve.py and NO C++ . The §2.1:631 slot-count remedy NAMES `--parallel`, which Task 12.1 (plan 2866-2889, NOT_STARTED) wires into serve.py itself; 12.2 asserts only that the remedy string names it.

assertions.text: the detection matrix, one fixture repo per ecosystem (package.json / CMakeLists.txt+enable_testing / pyproject.toml / Cargo.toml / go.mod), proposes verify scopes whose `command` is an argv ARRAY (never a shell string) and whose `itemTest` is the §2.1:499 default VERBATIM — node ['node','--test','{files}'], pytest ['pytest','{files}'], go ['go','test','{dirs}'], ctest ['ctest','-R','{name}'], cargo NO itemTest key at all — and each proposal is proven to fit the COMMITTED machinery rather than a parallel one: evidence.detectRunner(proposedCommand) returns the matching RUNNER_PROFILES entry for every non-cargo ecosystem, and evidence.substituteItemTest(proposedItemTest, testScope) returns a fully substituted argv with no '{' token left in it

the go proposal targets package DIRS and never test-function names: substituteItemTest(['go','test','{dirs}'], ['pkg/a/x_test.go','pkg/a/y_test.go','pkg/b/z_test.go']) === ['go','test','./pkg/a','./pkg/b'] (deduplicated, first-seen order, ./ prefixed), and NO proposed go argv anywhere in the matrix contains '-run'. This is the §2.1:503-506 correction the task bullet flags as previously missed: `-run` matches test FUNCTION names, so handed file basenames it silently exits 0 having run zero tests

the node leg reads the repo's package.json rather than assuming: with `scripts.test` present the proposed scope command is that script tokenized by core/shell-parse shellTokens, and the ['node','--test','{files}'] itemTest is attached ONLY when detectRunner(that command) is the node profile — so a `"test": "jest"` repo gets command ['jest'] and NO itemTest (the §2.1:487-497 absent-template fallback), while a `"test": "node --test"` repo gets both. With no scripts.test the proposal is ['node','--test'] plus the node itemTest. No fixture ever pairs a non-node command with the node template

a fixture holding BOTH package.json and CMakeLists.txt+enable_testing yields TWO distinctly-named scopes in verify.scopes (neither silently overwriting the other) and a verify.requiredScopes entry per scope whose pattern is that ecosystem's source glob; a single-ecosystem fixture yields ONE scope and requiredScopes [{pattern:'**', scopes:[<that scope>]}]. requiredScopes is never written as an empty array (which would validate cleanly while leaving every path unverified)

each detected ecosystem carries its §2.1:523-526 behavioralPaths PROPOSAL — node ['src/**','lib/**']; python ['<pkg>/**'] with <pkg> read from pyproject.toml's project name/packages; go ['**/*.go']; cmake ['src/**','include/**']; cargo ['src/**'] — returned as a proposal attached to the confirmation ask and NEVER written without an explicit answer (a run that supplies no behavioralPaths answer writes no config at all). The go proposal is the positive glob only, and the ask text NAMES the '**/*_test.go' caveat §2.1:525 asks for but Config's positive-glob string[] cannot express

the Cargo.toml fixture is detected and proposes command ['cargo','test'] with NO itemTest key and behavioralPaths ['src/**']; the written config still validates against SCHEMAS.Config; and NO fifth entry is added to evidence.RUNNER_PROFILES — detectRunner(['cargo','test']) falls through to the node profile (evidence.ts:137), which is recorded as the deliberate conservative bin, not a bug

no proposed scope object ever carries a `buildCommand`: every emitted scope's key set is exactly {command, timeoutMs} or {command, timeoutMs, itemTest}, asserted key-by-key, and core validate('Config', writtenConfig).ok is true. The trap is real — §2.1:483-485 describes buildCommand and adapter/evidence.ts:338-342 implements it, but core/types.ts:530-540 omits it under additionalProperties:false, so a config carrying it fails its own registered schema. Asserted directly: validate('Config', {...writtenConfig with a buildCommand spliced into one scope}).ok is FALSE

§2.1:628 — a proposed command whose argv[0] does not exist on this machine makes setup FAIL, and the failure message names the exact argv and a remedy (§2.1:634: a failure with a named remedy, never a warning); after the failure NO .conductor/config.json exists. The check covers every command the config would record: each scope command, each itemTest template substituted against a representative testScope file, and (on reconfigure) each format-rule command

the smoke check is a real spawn under the committed discipline, and its verdict is spawnability alone: (a) a command that EXISTS but exits non-zero on the probe PASSES — 'unspawnable' is the failure the plan names, not 'unhappy with its arguments'; (b) an argv[0] containing shell metacharacters (e.g. ['echo hi; rm -rf tmp']) is treated as ONE executable name, fails to spawn, and is never interpreted — proving shell:false; (c) the child runs under evidence.childEnv (a parent GIT_DIR/NODE_TEST_CONTEXT does not reach it) and is killed by a bounded timeout so no probe can wedge setup

§2.1:629 — against a stubbed GET {origin}/v1/models whose `data` omits the candidate models.default, setup FAILS and the message names the missing model id AND the ids the server did list; against a stub whose list contains it, this proof passes. The request is a direct bounded HTTP GET recorded by the stub, so the proof cannot pass vacuously by never being made

models.default is DERIVED, never guessed: with a stub serving exactly one model id, the written config's models.default is that id (and models.roles is {} per G13); with the caller supplying a model id, that id is used and checked against the list; with several ids served and no caller-supplied id, setup FAILS naming the ambiguity and the remedy (set models.default in .conductor/config.json) and writes nothing. No branch ever writes a hard-coded weight name

§2.1:630 — setup makes ONE tiny schema-constrained request as a direct POST {origin}/v1/chat/completions with stream:false and response_format json_schema (recorded on the stub, so the shape of the request is asserted, not assumed). A stubbed reply whose content does not validate against the probe's schema via core validate() FAILS setup naming the check; a conforming reply passes. The probe never goes through opencode's prompt path, which adapter/wire-notes.md:41-55 proved emits neither `format` nor `response_format` at 1.18.15

§2.1:631 — setup issues parallel.maxReaders concurrent trivial completions and measures OVERLAP: against a stub that serializes (it never holds more than maxReaders-1 requests open at once) setup FAILS and the message names the observed count, the configured maxReaders, and the `--parallel` remedy; against a stub that holds all N open simultaneously it passes. The measurement is of concurrency actually observed on the server side, not of wall-clock timing

setup dispatches ZERO model sub-sessions: across a full successful setup the fake SDK's ordered call log is empty, while the HTTP stub records the three proof requests. Every proof is a direct bounded request the handler makes itself — a setup proof that went through a model session could be answered by the model instead of by the server, which is the one thing these proofs exist to prevent

G5 — the proofs run against the origin resolveBaseUrl(routerCfg, upstreamCfg, failoverState) yields, and a DOWN router is never itself a setup failure: with a router origin that refuses connections and a healthy upstream stub, the first failed request records noteRouterFailure (useUpstream latched, journaled `failover` at warn) and the three proofs then complete against the UPSTREAM stub and setup SUCCEEDS. Setup fails only on what the proofs themselves prove false

ordering pin (the §2.1:620-624 literal reading rejected in specGaps): the proofs run against the candidate config in MEMORY and the atomic write happens only after every one of them passes. Asserted on each failure leg independently — unspawnable command, missing models.default, unconstrained schema reply, short slot count — that .conductor/config.json does not exist afterwards and readWorkspaceConfig(root) is null, so no gate ever opens on an unproven config

§2.1:622 + §6.2:1875 — a first call in a git repo with no answers returns BOTH undefaultable asks (git.mode, offering the three GIT_MODES; and the behavioralPaths confirmation, carrying the detected proposal) and writes NOTHING: no .conductor/config.json, no questions.jsonl record anywhere (adapter/questions.ts is never called — it needs a runDir setup has not got, and QUESTION_ORIGINS has no setup origin), and no widening of QUESTION_ORIGINS. The asks are the handler's RESULT, which is what makes them the sanctioned interactive ask rather than a §2.11 question

a call supplying only ONE of the two answers still writes nothing and re-returns the missing ask; neither value is ever silently defaulted. Asserted negatively too: over the whole fixture matrix, no written config exists whose git.mode or behavioralPaths was not explicitly answered — in particular no config is ever written carrying the §2.1:582 example git.mode 'commit' or the §2.1:527 example behavioralPaths ['src/**'] by default

§3.9:1500-1502 — in a workspace where gitio.isRepo is false, setup offers EXACTLY ONE choice (initialize a repo here | run in no-git mode), does not also ask the git.mode question (no-git forces it), and writes nothing until the choice is answered. Choosing 'initialize' performs `git init` from the HANDLER through gitio's execFileSync-argv discipline (never a model session, never a shell string), after which isRepo(root) is true and the SAME call continues down the ordinary git-repo path including the git.mode ask

choosing no-git writes a config with git.mode 'read-only' and parallel.writes 'off', performs NO .git/info/exclude registration (there is no .git), and — the load-bearing half — invents NO configuration field for it: the written object's key set is exactly SCHEMAS.Config's, validate('Config', written).ok is true, and there is no `noGit`, no publish flag and no worktree flag anywhere in it (configSchema's additionalProperties:false at types.ts:672 would reject one). No-git stays a RUNTIME gitio.isRepo derivation, which is the same thing the 9.5b publish refusal keys on

in a git repo, a completed setup registers `.conductor/` in .git/info/exclude through the COMMITTED adapter/state.ts registerConductorExclude (:214) and not a second implementation: the exclude file contains exactly one `.conductor/` line, a pre-existing unrelated line is preserved, and a second setup/reconfigure adds no duplicate. A setup that FAILS a proof registers nothing

a completed setup writes .conductor/config.json exactly once through adapter/state.ts writeFileAtomicSync (:136), and the file read back with readJsonFileSync satisfies validate('Config', …).ok === true. Its content is the confirmed answers merged over the §2.1 defaults: version 1; the detected verify.scopes and requiredScopes; format.rules []; the answered git.mode with branchPolicy 'pin' and preexistingDirty 'refuse'; and every §2.1:566-618 workflow / parallel / models / ponytail / retention / logging default present with the plan's value (trivialMaxFiles 2, planReviewers 4, planReviewMaxRounds 3, itemReviewers 6, skepticsPerFinding 2, reviewMaxRounds 3, vetCritics 3, vetMaxRounds 3, testRepairAttempts 3, debugFixCap 3, maxOverridesPerItem 1, maxOverridesPerRun 2, writes 'off', maxImplementers 2, maxReaders 6, subSessionTimeoutMs 900000, ponytail 'full', keepRuns 20, maxRunDirBytes 268435456, pruneOnRunCreate true, logging.level 'info')

adapter/state.ts gains ONE exported workspace-config reader and the repoConfigured derivation on top of it (there is none at HEAD — repoConfigured is only ever a parameter, gates-phase.ts:239 / inject.ts:94), and BOTH handleSetup and the caller that feeds legalTools consume that one function. It returns null/false for all three of: file absent, file unparseable, and file failing validate('Config') — so a corrupt config reopens setup instead of opening every gate on an unvalidated object. No fixture exists in which the gate treats the repo as configured while the handler treats it as unconfigured

handleSetup honours the Task 3.2 legality contract in both directions: it RUNS while .conductor/config.json is absent (the state where core/gates-phase.ts:246-253 legalizes only conductor_setup + conductor_status and recommends setup, and adapter/inject.ts already names it as the next action), and on an already-configured repo WITHOUT reconfigure:true it REFUSES, naming reconfigure:true as the legal alternative and writing nothing. Neither gates-phase.ts nor inject.ts is modified by this task — their committed tests still pass unchanged

conductor_setup {reconfigure:true} re-runs setup ONLY with no live run: with a persisted current run that core/stops.ts isTerminal reports false, reconfigure is DENIED naming the live run and the existing config is left byte-identical; with no current-run pointer, or one pointing at a terminal run (stop recorded, or state REPORTED/TRIVIAL_DONE/ANSWERED), it proceeds. The guard reads the persisted run rather than opening a workspace, since opening one would take the very lock it is testing for

a completed reconfigure journals a config DIFF — the changed keys with old and new values, and only the changed ones — through the injected sink, on a name inside the closed §7.4 vocabulary (core/journal-events.ts EVENTS.state widened by exactly one name under the file's own rule, the `decision.recorded` precedent), driven through the REAL throwing journal so an unlisted name would fail the test rather than pass silently. The record is emitted through a runId-OPTIONAL sink because setup has no run, and a reconfigure that changes nothing journals a diff with an empty change set rather than omitting the fact

C-003 binding: the pytest leg ships MEASURED on this machine, never assumed. Bare `pytest` is not on PATH (pytest 8.4.2 lives under /usr/bin/python3), so the pyproject fixture exercises BOTH legs for real — the §2.1:499 default ['pytest','{files}'] is tried first and its smoke spawn genuinely fails here, and the recorded fallback [<python3>,'-m','pytest','{files}'] genuinely spawns; the returned proposal names which form was chosen; and evidence.detectRunner on the fallback argv returns the pytest profile (evidence.ts:130-132), so nothing downstream sees a different runner

G1/G14 — the setup path adds no runtime dependency and nothing runtime-exclusive: a source scan of the new/edited adapter modules shows imports only of node: built-ins already used elsewhere in conductor/adapter (node:fs, node:path, node:child_process, node:http) and of conductor's own core/adapter modules, with no bare third-party specifier and no Bun-only or Node-only global. Setup must work under both runtimes for the same reason the rest of the suite does
